title: Internal Hom preserves integer-indexed product fans
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $A$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ be module sheaves and let $c$ be a limiting product fan with vertex $P$ and projections $\pi_i:P\to N_i$. Then the fan with vertex $\mathcal Hom_R(A,P)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and projections $\mathcal Hom_R(A,\pi_i)$ is limiting. No finiteness or local freeness is assumed.

proof.text: Module-sheaf evaluation preserves limits. Thus restricting the product to any slice gives a product fan, by the joint reflection of limits by presheaf evaluations. Each evaluation of the internal Hom has as elements the localized linear maps.

Given a test fan, lift each sectionwise family of localized maps into that slice product. Product uniqueness proves additivity and scalar compatibility; the scalar action on localized maps is postcomposition with the restrictions of the scalar. Product factorization gives the fan factorization law and product uniqueness gives the uniqueness law. Joint reflection of limits by presheaf evaluation and fully faithful sheaf forgetfulness give the claimed limit.
